reason: Umbrella for changing Metaform code. Four narrow project skills (ticket work, module verbs/settings, web page and browser tests, agent body embodiment) are all development work on the same repo with the same test and scope discipline. Each sibling's rules are carried whole into references/ and pointed at from a short labeled body. Re-staged with a description inside the 60-char index budget; the first attempt was rejected on description length.

Worker agents on tickets were refused op=add and need the note-based handoff; orchestrator instruction routes spec drafts to artifacts/specs-draft/; stale memory observations about a replaced design were left behind and had to be removed.

The dispatch_agent_options rewrite showed that one shared list setting drops entries on save; a settings-meaning change needed a migration and restart note; CLI completion needed discovery to run in the completer path.
The elicitation rule was missed because the description does not name agent questions, AskUserQuestion or dispatch. Widen the trigger so the skill loads for that work.

Rich's rule, 2026-10-14: workers must not put questions to the person. Elicitation had been left as the one route for agent questions to reach him after `map ask` was removed. The gate, the decide answer and the test setup are not in the skill, so the next session would restore the old behaviour.

A browser test started a system agent's runner and never stopped it. The run output then listed a leftover metaform dispatch process. Tests that start runners need an explicit stop, which the skill does not mention.
Mid-run, the ticket's task was replaced and the notice said not to restore the old question buttons. The agent had to re-read the ticket to get the new task. The skill has no rule for this.
Roundtable spend/rounds work hit both pitfalls: settings.number is int-only, and an agent could otherwise open a table past a person-only limit.
A throwaway check file failed collection until it carried a kind marker; the no-new-test-files rule in the person's CLAUDE.md should be stated next to it.
Strict pyright rejected a .get on an Any-typed reply; the cast-first fix passed and is the repeatable pattern.

Three lessons from the Space-to-talk ticket: (1) the browser check recipe for the web GUI (private server on a temp home, fake mic, CSP blocks string predicates, stubbed voice endpoints) was rediscovered by trial and error and is not in the skill; (2) a key that starts a mode must not leave focus in a text box, or the next press types; (3) the shared tree had someone else's uncommitted edits in keys.js, so the agent edited one line and did not commit. Patched into the existing web and tickets sections rather than a new skill. Description shortened to fit the index budget.

Ticket 67c956b9 found three browser-check pitfalls not in the reference: a Promise predicate in wait_for_function returns at once, pictures from a non-person camera show mirrored signs unless the labels are turned for that render, and the mascot body can be a bare Object3D with frames paused. Folded into the existing web browser-check reference and pointed to from the Web page section.

The VIEW-051 episode hit three repeatable web-page pitfalls: a depth filter applied in only one builder, a settings read that raced the async save (assert '3' == 'all'), and a 'node not found' console error that failed the problems check. None is in the skill yet.

Dispatch thread line numbering moved to a shared helper with a cursor gotcha and a silent-failure mode; the existing skill has no dispatch section and future edits to runner/serve would repeat the same mistakes.
The episode ran into a concurrent session editing the same test and runner files; the rule to re-read and to avoid file swaps is not in the skill yet.
Episode diagnosed a 'shared session' report from short ids that were only prefix-equal; the lesson is a durable debugging rule for dispatch and roundtable sessions.
Three test-authoring defects hit in one run (B023 loop capture, walrus-in-comprehension SyntaxError, a test inserted mid-function) each cost a rerun; the fixes belong with the existing test rules.
